title: Capturing Representative Hand Use at Home Using Egocentric Video in Individuals with Upper Limb Impairment
protocol: Obtain agreement of each participant on the recording schedules, after discussing any concerns that they may have.
Set a goal of 3 h of videos over two weeks.
Inform participants that insufficient videos may lead to extending their recording periods.
Instruct participants to focus on capturing realistic routines instead of specifying particular activities to record.
Ensure that participants understand that all recordings should take place inside their homes, not in public places to avoid privacy issues.
Give examples that may raise privacy concerns, such as bathing, dressing/undressing, and checking confidential information.
Remind participants to be aware of mirrors which may show their faces in recordings.
Suggest that participants avoid the presence of other people such as family members or caregivers as much as possible in videos.
Demonstrate how to use an egocentric camera (Table of Materials) to participants.
Demonstrate how to turn the camera on and off.
Demonstrate how to control recordings (start, pause, stop) using the camera.
Demonstrate how to turn on and off the tablet.
Demonstrate how to connect the tablet to the camera through the camera app.
Demonstrate how to control the recordings from the camera app.
Demonstrate how to review recorded videos from the camera app.
Demonstrate how to trim or delete the videos from the camera app.
Place the camera on the participant's forehead.
Adjust the headband to wear the camera comfortably and steadily.
Ensure an optimal angle of the camera with respect to the forehead.
Record a short video segment while moving hands in front and manipulating an object.
Ensure both hands are clearly visible in the central region during manipulation tasks.
Practice using the camera and tablet with participants until proficiency is demonstrated.
Provide participants with a kit containing all necessary equipment for recording ADLs at home.
Include extra batteries, chargers, cables, headband, and guidelines in the kit.
Offer contact information to researchers for troubleshooting during home recordings.
Follow up with participants after one week by calling to document progress and resolve issues.
Retrieve all equipment and videos from participants either in person or via pre-paid mail parcels.
Ensure participants agree to share all returned videos with the research team.
Encourage participants to review collected videos before returning them, deleting any unwanted portions.
For research studies, review returned videos.
Check if anyone appears in the video without having given their consent.
Send consent forms or call individuals who appear in the videos to gain their consents for use of the videos.
If individuals are not reachable, delete portions of the videos in which they appear.
